themes_detail.label: Street Signs Vanishing
themes_detail.summary: Street sign complaints exploded to 9 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 0.2 per week—a 3,500% spike (z-score: 20.21)—suggesting either coordinated theft, contractor error, or systemic removal across Murray Hill/Gramercy that warrants immediate DOT investigation.
evidence: 9 street sign complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 per-week baseline over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 20.21)
Highest z-score spike in entire dataset, indicating statistical anomaly
Concentrated in single week, suggesting acute event rather than chronic issue
reporting_angles: Contact DOT to determine if signs were removed for construction, theft, or maintenance failure; map the geographic concentration
Interview residents about navigation and safety impacts; check if this correlates with any active street work or contractor activity

themes_detail.label: Cannabis Retailers Under Fire
themes_detail.summary: Cannabis retailer complaints jumped to 3 THIS WEEK from a baseline of 0.1 per week—a 2,300% spike—indicating residents may be raising concerns about illegal shops, improper licensing, or operating violations in the district.
evidence: 3 cannabis retailer complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 per-week baseline (z-score: 8.69, severity: high)
Represents second-largest spike by z-score in dataset
Follows broader NYC legalization and enforcement debates
reporting_angles: Identify which specific shops triggered complaints; determine if they are licensed legal retailers or unlicensed operations
Interview DOE and DCWP on enforcement priorities and complaints; speak with residents about what violations concern them most

themes_detail.label: Street Conditions Deteriorating Fast
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints spiked to 54 THIS WEEK from a 21.1 per-week average—a 156% increase (z-score: 3.54)—suggesting pothole, sidewalk, or pavement failures may be accelerating in Murray Hill/Gramercy this week.
evidence: 54 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 21.1 per-week average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 3.54)
156% increase concentrated in current week—sharp, acute spike
Part of broader winter/seasonal pattern but magnitude of this week's jump notable
reporting_angles: Request DOT repair data and prioritization queues; map hotspots of complaints to identify worst blocks
Interview residents and local business owners about specific street failures (potholes, cracked sidewalks) and impact on foot traffic and deliveries

themes_detail.label: Taxi Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Taxi report complaints jumped to 5 THIS WEEK from a baseline of 0.5 per week—a 900% spike (z-score: 6.36)—suggesting a concentrated incident or enforcement surge affecting for-hire vehicle operations in the district.
evidence: 5 taxi report complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 per-week baseline (z-score: 6.36, severity: high)
900% spike magnitude suggests concentrated incident rather than slow trend
Complements existing For Hire Vehicle Complaint volume (305 complaints over 90 days)
reporting_angles: Contact TLC to identify what triggered spike: illegal cabs, service disruption, congestion complaint, or specific incident
Interview residents and business owners about their taxi experiences and any visible enforcement activity this week

themes_detail.label: Asbestos Complaints Climbing
themes_detail.summary: Asbestos complaints rose to 5 LAST WEEK from a baseline of 1.0 per week—a 400% spike (z-score: 5.66)—potentially indicating construction, renovation, or demolition activity releasing or disturbing asbestos-containing materials in older buildings.
evidence: 5 asbestos complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.0 per-week baseline (z-score: 5.66, severity: high)
400% spike coincides with high DOB alteration filing activity (989 alterations filed in last 90 days, 1,077 total permits)
Murray Hill/Gramercy contains many pre-1970s buildings likely to contain asbestos
reporting_angles: Cross-reference asbestos complaints with DOB permit data to identify buildings undergoing renovation; verify proper abatement procedures
Interview NYC Department of Environmental Protection and building residents about asbestos disclosure and safe renovation practices in the district
